title: Decreasing involutions and $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$-means
summary: An $n$-mean on a topological space $X$ is a continuous symmetric map $p\colon X^n\to X$ satisfying $p(x,\ldots,x)=x$ for every $x\in X$. If $X$ is a $G$-space, such an $n$-mean is equivariant if $p(gx_1,\ldots,gx_n)=g p(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ for every $g\in G$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in X$. For finite $G$, we prove that, in the presence of an equivariant $n$-mean with $n$ a multiple of $\lvert G\rvert$, the $\mathrm{ANE}$, $\mathrm{AE}$, and $\mathrm{AR}$ properties imply their equivariant counterparts. We next consider $\mathbb Z_2$-actions induced by decreasing involutions on topological lattices.…
